spine.rule: One owner per capability. EXTEND the owner; CREATE only with a written reason; a second implementation exists only behind an interface declared here.

modules.purpose: Prepare, supervise and independently verify one fail-closed Rhino .3dm export of an exact compiled program.
owns: RhinoCadProgramBinding and RhinoCadExportIdentity: the P036 record/branch/stage identity an export is bound to
the immutable export plan: workspace layout, script, completion token, host witness and the full validation denominator digest
the STA PowerShell/COM worker source and its shell-free encoded command
supervising the blocking worker, collecting its output, and independently cleaning the Rhino host it started
readback verification: the saved file's physical objects, semantics, bounds, counts, layer colours and document user text against the denominator
the execution receipt and its status
does_not_own: translating the program into a script - adapters.cad_program
selecting what a patch rebuilds - adapters.cad_patch
reading the .3dm - adapters.three_dm_inspector
writing anything into the project repository - it has no project-repository or canonical-write authority; runtime.project_runner retains the receipt
choosing the workspace - the caller supplies an existing speculative workspace
invariants: a successful process exit is never sufficient - the saved file is read back independently and must match the denominator
the export identity refuses any up_axis but Z-up and any unit outside millimeter/meter/inch/foot
every path is constrained to the caller-supplied workspace; no shell interpolation and no launcher file exists
the plan is immutable once prepared and identified by its plan digest
discovery is read-only: it never launches or attaches to Rhino
modules.notes: Imports CompiledGeometryProgram through the runtime/geometry_compiler shim; that import moves to compilers.geometry when the shim goes.

modules.purpose: Diff two compiled programs into the closed set of operations a Rhino rebuild must redo, and the prelude that carries the rest of the prior document forward.
owns: per-object structural digests of what the CAD script actually emits
the diff into changed / added / retired / kept object ids, with a reason per object
closing the rebuild set over input edges (consumers of a rebuilt object, producers of a rebuilt operation's inputs)
the Rhino-side prelude that opens the prior model, deletes the retired objects and re-stamps the kept ones
refusing a patch that cannot be expressed, so the caller rebuilds instead
does_not_own: emitting the rebuilt operations - adapters.cad_program's operation_subset does
running or verifying the patched export - adapters.cad_execution
deciding whether to patch at all - runtime.project_runner's _export chooses reuse, patch or rebuild
comparing two runs' saved geometry - studio.validation's compare
invariants: an object is rebuilt only when its structural digest or its analytic bounds actually changed, beyond tolerance
the rebuild set is closed over input edges - nothing consumed or produced by a rebuilt operation is left stale
an inexpressible patch fails CadPatchError, which is a signal to rebuild, never a partial document
modules.notes: P103 incremental export; the only reason a run may reuse a prior .3dm.

modules.purpose: Translate a compiled neutral geometry program into one deterministic, semantics-carrying rhinoscriptsyntax build script, plus the analytic denominator it must reproduce.
owns: the supported operation vocabulary and its rhinoscriptsyntax emission (solid, revolve, extrusion, loft, boolean union/difference/intersection, linear and radial array, transform, curve)
the layer path and layer colour tables derived from components and material assignment
the archflow:* object user text each physical object must carry (expected_object_semantics)
the analytic per-object bounds the realization must reproduce (expected_object_bounds)
applying a datum-bound base_level to profile points (lift_to_base_level)
the P103 partial emission of an operation subset
does_not_own: running the script, saving the file or verifying the readback - adapters.cad_execution
deciding which operations a patch rebuilds - adapters.cad_patch
reading the resulting .3dm - adapters.three_dm_inspector
compiling the program - compilers.geometry
any design decision: it holds no design authority and adds no geometry
outputs: CadTranslation (script, physical object ids, losses, layer colours)
invariants: an unsupported operation kind fails CadTranslationError rather than being dropped silently
the same program translates to the same script bytes - the emission is deterministic and self-contained
coordinates pass through as the program states them; the translator performs no frame conversion
every physical object is named and carries its archflow:* identity strings
modules.notes: The single CAD translation on the spine; P107's in-process OCCT executor would be a second executor of this program, not a second translation.

modules.purpose: Invoke one explicitly configured JSON model command as a detached, bounded subprocess and return a typed invocation receipt.
owns: ModelProviderSpec: the command, protocol, timeouts, byte and token caps, isolation flag, and the spec fingerprint
the async subprocess invocation with its input/output byte limits and timeout
decoding the command's answer (including codex exec JSONL) into ArchFlowModelOutput@1
the Codex CLI configuration and its detached, tool-free prompt
turning a failure into a typed receipt status rather than an exception
does_not_own: the request/receipt contracts themselves - ports.model
authority, envelopes and provider lifecycle - production.provider_runtime and production.responsibility
what the model is asked to author - capabilities.geometry_proposal
any project write, workspace handle or world mutation, and any fallback provider
invariants: no shell and no fallback: exactly one explicitly configured command is executed
input and output are hard-capped in bytes; exceeding a cap is a typed failure receipt
the adapter holds no authority token - it is bound behind one by production.provider_runtime
modules.notes: The concrete AsyncModelProvider on the spine; a live provider still enters through provider_runtime.

modules.purpose: Read one .3dm file headlessly and return a deterministic, JSON-compatible summary of what is actually saved in it.
owns: the ThreeDmInspection shape and its versioned key sets (the one place the schema's required keys are declared)
reading layers, objects, instance definitions and references, counts by type and by layer
document and object user strings
world bounds: aggregate, per named object, and the visible-bounds witnesses that back each leaf bound
native material and render-material tables and each object's material binding
per-object encoded-geometry digests and morphology analysis (planarity, curve sampling)
the typed, fail-closed inspection error codes
does_not_own: producing the file - adapters.cad_execution
deciding whether the file matches a program - adapters.cad_execution's readback verification
importing RhinoCommon, starting Rhino, or choosing where anything is persisted
comparing two inspections - studio.validation's compare
invariants: read-only: rhino3dm is imported lazily, one immutable byte snapshot is read, and no Rhino process is started
bounds come from saved visible geometry, never from Brep control points
an object geometry digest hashes encoded geometry only - object attributes cannot change it
an unreadable or unsupported file fails with a named error code, not a partial summary
modules.notes: The single source of the inspection key sets that viewers and readback both check against.

modules.purpose: Define and gate the mandatory typed decisions a stage requires, and compile the gate-passed ones into hard commitments.
owns: DeclarationQuadrant and DeclarationKind: the vocabulary a stage's decision fields are grouped and typed by
DeclarationField and StageDeclarationContract, with each field's unit, authorized range and range provenance
the deterministic geometry cross-checks that bind a declared value to the accepted massing
the fail-closed stage gate over a declaration set (validate_stage_declarations)
compiling gate-passed declarations of named quadrants into HARD Commitments
selecting exactly the decision basis shards a contract's fields need
does_not_own: storing declared field values - the framework holds contracts, the provider supplies values
the commitment lifecycle and validation - archflow.state.commitments and archflow.validation
which seat may declare in which quadrant - capabilities.discipline_seats
stage opening or closure - archflow.state.stage_workflow and control.stage_closure
invariants: the gate fails closed: a missing, out-of-range or geometry-contradicted field blocks the stage
a declared value is checked against the massing by a deterministic measure, within the contract's tolerance ratio
only gate-passed declarations become commitments, and only in the quadrants named
modules.notes: On the spine today mainly through DeclarationQuadrant, which scopes what a seat may declare.

modules.purpose: Divide authoring across role-scoped seats: what a seat may write, what it may read, what it hands the next seat, and in which round it runs.
owns: SeatSpec: the component subtrees a seat writes, its disciplines, phases, quadrants, the seats it consumes and whether it reviews
the owned subtree and ancestor computation over the component tree
compiling a deterministic SeatHandover from a committed seat: its datums, exclusion bounds, digests and object constraints
projecting the design state onto one seat as SeatAuthoringContext, so sibling subtrees never leak
refusing a seat that publishes a datum over a project level or grid axis
checking declared engagements against a handover's exclusion bounds
scheduling seats into parallel rounds by handover dependency
does_not_own: producing any geometry inside a seat's scope - capabilities.element_producers
running the rounds, exporting or writing seat records - runtime.project_runner
the declaration contract and its gate - capabilities.declaration
who is authorized to write canonically - archflow.contracts.authority (seats carry no_authority)
reading the project's authored seat pack from disk - studio.candidate's seats adapter and tools/run_project.py
invariants: a seat's authoring context contains only its subtree, its ancestors and the handovers it consumes - a sibling subtree is never visible
a handover is bound to the base state digest it was compiled from and carries its own digest
a seat may not publish a datum id that a project level or grid axis already owns
entering another seat's exclusion bound is a violation unless a DeclaredEngagement is on record
seats carry explicit no_authority for canonical write, design and stage acceptance
modules.notes: P095/P098; seats are people, not state - they arrive beside the record, never inside it.

modules.purpose: Turn a State Record's Element@1 rows into geometry operations, datum bindings, published datums and materialized relations, reading references rather than computing coordinates.
owns: the producer dispatch table PRODUCERS: column-array, capitals, beam, pediment, wall, prism, ring, loft, dome-cap, declined
reading Element@1 entities off a StateRecord into ElementRow, in production order
topological production order: an element that names another (or its published `<id>-top`) is produced after it
publishing `<id>-top` interface datums an element grants to what it supports
declaring the support relations that construction materializes (ProducedRelation), with engagement or rise
typed declination: a component owned, looked at, and left without geometry for a stated reason
the building-local frame id and the +Y extrusion convention every producer emits
does_not_own: turning a reference into a plan coordinate or an elevation datum - capabilities.reference_resolver
the wall solid, its through-cuts and its hosted voids - capabilities.wall_solver
window and door member geometry inside a void - capabilities.opening_solver
resolving a symbolic datum binding into a number - compilers.geometry
measuring whether a declared relation actually holds - capabilities.relation_checks
which rows a seat may produce, and the seat's exclusions - runtime.project_runner and capabilities.discipline_seats
invariants: no producer computes a plan coordinate itself; every position goes through resolve_plan
elevations leave as (datum id, offset) bindings, never as literal numbers
an element referencing another is produced after it; a reference cycle or a missing element fails ElementProducerError
an unknown producer name fails typed rather than being skipped
an overlap into a support exists only as a declared ENGAGEMENT parameter, recorded on the relation
modules.notes: The single geometry-emission owner on the spine; P105 is where monument vocabulary would be added here rather than beside it.

modules.purpose: Author, compile and retain bounded rounds of a provider's neutral geometry proposal against one exact state, with no fallback and no acceptance authority.
owns: the strict provider request and response contracts (the authoring output topology and its function contracts)
the bounded round loop, its policy knobs (round cap, bookkeeping completion, progress budget, partial acceptance, stall escalation) and its resume seam
decoding a provider's full or edit-shaped answer into a typed GeometryProgramProposal without inventing geometry
semantic coverage validation of a proposal against the state, commitments, seat scope and required component bindings
the lineage / round / proposal / deferral / escalation records and their persistence through the repository
reloading one exact compiled program from its retained record
does_not_own: compiling the proposal into objects and digests - compilers.geometry
invoking the model provider or signing its receipt - ports.model and production.provider_runtime
accepting a stage or writing canonical state - it holds no hard-gate or canonical-write authority
producing geometry from records itself - capabilities.element_producers (the runner feeds it an authored proposal)
any CAD translation or execution - archflow.adapters
invariants: no fallback: a round that does not compile is rejected with issues, never patched into acceptance
the provider receipt's identity must match the declared GeometryProposalProviderIdentity
the proposal is bound to one exact design-state digest and predecessor program digest
a round is capped by policy; exhausting the cap deposits a deferral or escalation record, not a result
every round is retained before the next one is authored
modules.notes: The runner drives it with an inline RecordedProposalProvider for replay; a live provider enters through production.provider_runtime.

modules.purpose: Fill a wall's hosted voids with window and door types, emitting frame, glazing and leaf members as one hosted assembly per opening.
owns: WindowType and DoorType: the proportions of one opening family (frame width/depth/projection, glazing or leaf thickness, offsets, leaf count and clearances)
solving a void into frame members, a pane, or jambs/head plus one or two leaves
the arrayed form: one member definition placed void.count times along the wall
assembling the members into a HostedAssembly with its roles and interface reference
does_not_own: where the opening is, how big it is, or which storey it belongs to - capabilities.wall_solver's HostedVoid says
cutting the host - capabilities.wall_solver owns the tool and the boolean
choosing which type an opening gets - capabilities.element_producers maps opening id to type
any project coordinate or level elevation
invariants: a type carries proportions only - no position, no level, no absolute size
every member is placed relative to the void the wall granted
a void whose opening id has no type fails OpeningSolverError rather than being left empty
modules.notes: P092 filler side; P099 gives the arrayed placement so N identical openings share one member definition.

modules.purpose: Resolve the record's symbolic plan and elevation references against grids, levels and host lines - the one resolver every producer calls.
owns: the reference vocabulary: GridRef, GridIntersection, AxisPoint, HostAlong, LevelRef, OffsetFrom
parsing a reference from its JSON form
resolving a plan reference to one (x, z) coordinate
resolving an elevation reference to a symbolic (level datum id, offset) pair
ReferenceContext: the grids, levels and host lines a resolver may read
HostLine: a host element's reference line and points along/across it
does_not_own: emitting any geometry operation from a resolved point - capabilities.element_producers
publishing a datum an element grants - capabilities.element_producers
substituting a datum id for its numeric elevation - compilers.geometry
the ProjectLevels / ProjectGrids record shapes themselves - archflow.state.geometry_program
derivation expressions - archflow.state.derivation
invariants: resolve_elevation never returns a number - the compiler is the only thing that turns a datum id into one
an unknown axis, level or host fails ReferenceError rather than defaulting
a resolver reads only grids, levels and host lines; it cannot see components or geometry
modules.notes: The datum namespace boundary: level ids and element-top ids resolve here, so producers stay coordinate-free.

modules.purpose: Measure a State Record's relations against realized geometry and record held / violated / unchecked as a RelationCheckReport@1.
owns: the checker table keyed by a relation's validator check_kind (today only support_contact)
the support-contact measurement: subject top against object bottom plus declared engagement or rise, and against a named datum
the element-standing-on-a-level orientation of the same check
reporting a relation with no validator or no checker as `unchecked` rather than as passing
the report's three-state counts, held / fully_checked flags and its digest
does_not_own: which relations reach the check - runtime.project_runner filters the record to kind `support` before calling
producing the geometry or the analytic bounds it measures - capabilities.element_producers and compilers.geometry
declaring the relation in the first place - archflow.state.state_record
turning a violation into a stage or run verdict - runtime.project_runner
any repair or healing of geometry that fails a check - nothing on the spine does this
invariants: nothing is healed: a check only measures and reports
`held` alone is not a green light - an unchecked relation does not count against it, so held must be shown with fully_checked
a relation whose objects have no realized bounds fails RelationCheckError instead of being scored
the report carries the record digest it was measured against
modules.notes: One checker per kind the record can declare; adding a kind means adding a checker here, not a check elsewhere.

modules.purpose: Solve one wall from its location line, thickness, height and storey datum into a solid, a cut tool per opening, and the hosted voids openings are filled into.
owns: WallElement geometry: reference line, normal, plan points and plan rectangles in wall coordinates
OpeningRequest: where an opening sits along the wall, its width, sill, head and repeat count/step
enumerating the wall solid, one tool per opening and the single boolean difference that cuts them
granting each opening a HostedVoid - its aperture in wall coordinates plus the object ids it may use
rejecting overlapping openings, openings past the wall ends, and openings that hit a declared exclusion
does_not_own: what fills a void - capabilities.opening_solver decides frames, panes and leaves
where the wall is in the project - capabilities.reference_resolver resolves its two plan references
the storey elevation as a number - the wall carries a base level datum id, resolved by compilers.geometry
reading opening requests off the record - capabilities.element_producers
invariants: the wall is one solid; every opening is a void request the wall hosts, never a separate subtraction chain
an opening's position is expressed in wall coordinates (along, across), never in project coordinates
a contract violation - non-positive size, an opening outside the wall, overlapping voids - fails WallSolverError
modules.notes: P092 host side: the wall grants the aperture, the opening type never moves it.

modules.purpose: The one pure compiler: bind a neutral geometry proposal to an exact state, order its operations, digest its objects, or return an explicit rejection receipt.
owns: the operation dependency graph, its deterministic order and per-object digests
frame, component and semantic-binding digests that bind a program to one state
resolving DatumBinding references into literal parameters (the only place a datum id becomes a number)
asset resolution and the substitution receipt when a requested asset is replaced
assembly role validation and revision preconditions against a prior program
the typed issue vocabulary and the compile receipt whose status is ACCEPTED or a rejection
does_not_own: authoring or repairing a proposal - capabilities.geometry_proposal
producing operations from records - capabilities.element_producers
any CAD script, execution or readback - archflow.adapters
persisting the program - the caller writes it through archflow.project.repository
accepting a stage - it holds no acceptance authority
invariants: pure: it reads inputs and returns a result, and never writes or mutates anything
a structurally invalid input raises; a semantically rejected proposal returns a receipt with issues and no program
every issue is appended, not short-circuited, so one round reports every independent failure
the compiled program is bound to the state digest and, on a revision, to the predecessor program digest
operation order is deterministic for one proposal
modules.notes: Named canonical in CANONICAL_SPINE 2.2 'Program and compiler'; runtime/geometry_compiler.py is only its shim.

modules.purpose: The single source of the all-False authority-flag block that every retained record carries.
owns: the default authority field names (DEFAULT_AUTHORITY_FIELDS)
constructing a key-sorted, all-False authority block (no_authority)
rejecting a malformed, duplicated or non-'_authority' field name (AuthorityContractError)
does_not_own: deciding which record needs which flags (each writer passes its field list)
enforcing that a producer really holds no authority (a static scan in the test suite holds the inline-block count at a baseline)
record serialization (each record type)
outputs: dict[str, bool] with every value False
invariants: every returned flag is exactly False
field names are lowercase identifiers ending in _authority
output keys are sorted, so canonical serialization is independent of caller order
modules.notes: fold: marked '← fold' in the move list; the hand-inlined authority blocks it replaced are still counted at a recorded baseline by a static test scan.

modules.purpose: Deterministic finite-JSON encoding and the sha-256 primitives every record digest on the spine is built from.
owns: canonical JSON text with sorted keys, no NaN/Infinity and no cycles (canonical_json)
its UTF-8 bytes and lowercase sha-256 (canonical_json_bytes, canonical_digest)
the 64-hex digest validator (require_sha256)
typed rejection of values that cannot be canonical JSON (CanonicalValueError)
does_not_own: excluding a record's own digest field before digesting (project.digests)
record file bytes on disk, which add a trailing newline (project.repository)
which fields a given record digests (each record type decides)
invariants: a pure function of the value: no filesystem, no clock, no randomness
ascii=True and ascii=False digest differently, so a record keeps the form it was written in
a non-finite float, a non-string mapping key or a cycle raises rather than being coerced
modules.notes: state/geometry_program.py re-implements this as digest_value/require_sha256 rather than importing it: a second digest implementation still on the spine.

modules.purpose: Strict scalar and deterministic-tuple validators shared by the newer typed contracts.
owns: bounded, trimmed, non-empty text (text)
enum-instance and finite-number checks (enum_value, finite_number)
exact mapping key-set checks used to detect schema drift (exact_mapping)
payload field primitives: mapping, list_of, tuple_of, typed_tuple, string_tuple, unique, number, positive, refs, ids
scheme-qualified logical-ref syntax, rejecting file: and drive-letter paths (logical_ref)
sorted-unique bounded tuples of refs and identifiers (deterministic_refs, deterministic_identifiers)
does_not_own: identifier syntax itself, which it delegates to project.refs.require_identifier
the logical-ref validator used by the operational-state family (state.operational_state.require_logical_ref is a parallel)
digesting or serializing the values it validates (contracts.canonical)
inputs: arbitrary value plus a field name
invariants: a tuple field must already be sorted and unique; the validator never sorts on the caller's behalf
collections are bounded at 4096 items
validation is total: an unexpected type raises rather than being coerced
modules.notes: Canonical, but all four of its consumers are themselves fold targets and no test imports it directly; finite_number is never imported.

modules.purpose: Own the provider-independent model invocation contracts: request, receipt, status, phase and the AsyncModelProvider Protocol.
owns: ModelInvocationRequest@1 and ModelInvocationReceipt@1, their serde and their schema refs
ModelPhase and ModelInvocationStatus
the AsyncModelProvider Protocol every provider satisfies
the payload validation that keeps a request and receipt portable and JSON-exact
does_not_own: executing anything - adapters.model_provider
authority, envelopes, signing or lifecycle - production.responsibility and production.provider_runtime
what a payload means - capabilities.geometry_proposal defines the authoring contract carried inside it
invariants: a request is bound to a checkpoint digest and a context digest; nothing is invoked without both
a receipt's output is either absent or matched by its output_sha256
contracts only - no module-level execution, no I/O
modules.notes: MODEL_REQUEST_CONTRACT / MODEL_RECEIPT_CONTRACT in provider_runtime are these classes' SCHEMA strings.

modules.purpose: Activate any model provider behind the P053 responsibility contract, so a live provider is reachable only through a signed envelope and a lifecycle receipt.
owns: the model responsibility contract definition (request and receipt schema refs)
binding an AsyncModelProvider into a handler that keeps the production authority token in a trusted closure
AuthorizedAsyncModelProvider: the only surface a caller sees after envelope validation
activation from an explicit identity, from a ModelProviderSpec, or as the Codex Agent CLI
the bounded in-process collector of already-validated invocation envelopes
does_not_own: the control plane, tokens, signing and lifecycle state machine - production.responsibility
executing the command - adapters.model_provider
the request and receipt contracts - ports.model
the replay provider the runner uses instead of a live one - runtime.project_runner's RecordedProposalProvider
invariants: the model adapter never sees the authority token - it stays in the binding closure
every returned receipt came out of an envelope the router validated
activation always produces a lifecycle receipt and a handover decision; there is no unqualified live provider
modules.notes: CANONICAL_SPINE 2.2 keeps this as the only door for a live provider; the archived portfolio lane re-enters through it.

modules.purpose: The P053 responsibility control plane: who may act for a responsibility, under what authority epoch, and with what signed, verifiable envelope.
owns: ResponsibilityContract, ProviderIdentity, ProviderRegistration and their digests
the lifecycle state machine (provider modes, qualification, handover decision and receipt, authority epoch)
ProductionAuthorityToken and its grant nonce and signature
InvocationEnvelope: a provider receipt plus the authority that produced it, signed and validated
the split capability surface: ResponsibilityRouter (register, resolve, invoke, validate) versus ResponsibilityReconciler (qualify, activate)
portability enforcement: safe ids, schema refs, and refusal of machine-local paths in payloads
shadow invocation of a non-active provider
does_not_own: any model-specific contract or execution - ports.model and adapters.model_provider
the model responsibility definition and its convenience activations - production.provider_runtime
what a receipt payload means - the capability that authored the request
persistence: it is in-process state, retained by whoever holds the envelope
invariants: lifecycle mutation is a separate object capability from invocation - a router holder cannot activate a provider
a handover is refused unless the caller's expected binding digest matches the current state (compare-and-swap on authority)
an envelope is signed over the authority token and the receipt digest, and validated before any receipt is trusted
a payload carrying a machine-local path or an unsafe id is refused
an invocation by a provider that is not the active one is refused unless it is an explicit shadow call
modules.notes: Generic over request/receipt types; the model responsibility is one instantiation, not a special case.

modules.purpose: The one semantic digest of canonical project-state content, taken with the state's own declared digest field removed.
owns: digesting canonical state content excluding state_sha256 (project_state_sha256)
verifying a declared state_sha256 against the recomputed digest
does_not_own: canonical JSON encoding and the raw sha-256 primitive (contracts.canonical)
the byte digest of a written record file, which includes a trailing newline (project.repository)
invariants: a declared state_sha256 that disagrees with the content raises
the digest is over content without its own digest field, so it is stable under re-declaration
never writes the filesystem
modules.notes: 31 lines; it is the seam between the semantic content digest and the repository's byte digest, which differ by a trailing newline.

modules.purpose: Pure mapping from a project root and identifiers to filesystem paths, with no directory creation and no writes.
owns: the on-disk names of a project's areas (project.json, HEAD, objects/sha256, events, canonical, runs, exports, input)
the run subdirectory names (RunLayout: run.json, records, branches, candidates, reviews, workspaces, recovery)
resolving a project-relative path or a record/artifact ref to an absolute path inside the root
does_not_own: creating directories or writing files (project.repository)
reference validity (project.refs)
locating an existing project root (project.location)
invariants: never creates a directory and never writes
a resolved path that escapes the project root raises
a ref belonging to another project is refused
modules.notes: Sole importer is project/repository.py and no test imports it directly; it is covered only through tests/test_project_repository.py. RunLayout is returned by ProjectLayout.run but never imported by name.

modules.purpose: Read-only resolution of where an existing project repository physically lives, and the single helper that opens it.
owns: the deterministic authority order local then relocated then workspace (locate_project)
relocation anchor validation by file digest (ProjectLocation, ProjectLocationKind)
checking that the manifest at a candidate root carries the requested project_id (ProjectLocationError)
the one open-by-project-id entry point (open_located_project)
does_not_own: creating a project or writing state (project.repository)
path names inside a project (project.layout)
manifest parsing (project.manifest)
invariants: never creates directories and never writes state
a relocation anchor whose digest disagrees is rejected rather than followed
a root whose project.json names another project is rejected
modules.notes: ProjectLocation is returned but never imported by name; the only non-test consumer is the Studio binding module.

modules.purpose: The immutable project.json identity and format-version record.
owns: project identity on disk (ProjectManifest.project_id)
the ArchFlowProject@1 schema and its exact field set
format_version as a positive integer
typed rejection of a drifted or incomplete manifest (ProjectManifestError)
does_not_own: reading or writing project.json (project.repository, project.location)
what a format version implies for snapshot shape (project.repository)
invariants: the manifest carries no mutable state: exactly schema, project_id and format_version
a missing or unknown field is an error, never a default
modules.notes: No dedicated test; the one test that imports ProjectManifest does so as a fixture, and real coverage comes through tests/test_project_repository.py.

modules.purpose: Persistence port protocols and the validated destination a producer must be handed before it is allowed to write anything.
owns: the persistence area vocabulary (PersistenceArea)
a validated project- or run-scoped write destination (PersistenceDestination)
the fail-closed check that a producer was assigned a destination (require_destination, PersistenceDestinationRequired)
the structural protocols a repository satisfies (RecordSink, ArtifactSink, CanonicalRepository, ProjectLoader)
does_not_own: any implementation of these ports (project.repository is the only one)
the filesystem path an area maps to (project.layout)
record content or schema (each record type)
invariants: a run-scoped area requires run_id and a project-scoped area forbids it
branch_id belongs only to the RUN_BRANCH area
nothing here writes; P035 deliberately supplies no filesystem writer
a producer without a destination stops and raises rather than choosing a location
modules.notes: ArtifactSink, CanonicalRepository and ProjectLoader are declared but no module imports them by name; only PersistenceArea/PersistenceDestination/require_destination/RecordSink are actually used.

modules.purpose: Defines the four stable identity types (project version, run, branch, record, artifact) and the portable identifier and path validators the whole spine reuses.
owns: branch equality checks (require_exact_branch, require_same_branch)
branch identity as run + branch_id + epoch (BranchRef)
content-addressed record and artifact references and their project:// uri (ProjectRecordRef, ProjectArtifactRef)
portable identifier syntax (require_identifier)
project version identity with its optional canonical state digest (ProjectVersionRef, require_digest)
project-relative path syntax, normalization and escape refusal (require_project_relative_path)
run identity bound to its base version (RunRef)
serialising and parsing the four references (to_dict/from_dict, record_ref_from_uri)
does_not_own: serializing a BranchRef to and from a dict (contracts.branch)
digesting content (contracts.canonical)

modules.notes: CANONICAL_SPINE 2.1 makes this the door live-model authoring re-enters by: typed intent, then record, then runner.

modules.purpose: Assemble the FastAPI application: settings in, routes mounted under /api, one error body out, and the reserved application ports.
owns: create_app and the uvicorn entry point, and the lifespan that lets a running candidate finish
StudioSettings and every environment variable the process reads (project dir, rhino export, workers, powershell, reference run)
the one error body {code, detail} plus question and acceptedForms, and the handlers that force every failure - including a bug - into it
the reserved application Protocols (IntentProvider, RetrievalProvider, PreviewBackend, ViewerAssetProvider, HumanReviewPort, StudioEventSink)
every wire DTO and its camelCase aliases, and the router mounting order
GET /api/health
does_not_own: any design question or kernel call
binding the project - studio.binding does that on first use, never at app creation
application behaviour behind any route - studio.binding, studio.intent, studio.candidate, studio.validation, studio.artifacts
implementations of the reserved ports: no port may waive validation or write canonical state
inputs: application values needing a wire shape
invariants: create_app touches no filesystem and binds no project - a wrong project root is discovered by the request that needs it
the project root is never defaulted in code
every failure answers in the same body shape, and an unexpected error says nothing about itself
ports.py holds Protocols only: there are deliberately no implementations here
projectBound in health is whether the binding opens, not a claim about what it contains
modules.notes: transport/* carries the wire shapes for all six concerns, so a DTO change is a shell change, not an application one.

modules.purpose: Say what a finished candidate validates to - the kernel's receipt - and, separately, whether it may advance and what refuses it.
owns: building the CandidateSubmission and asking archflow.validation.engine.validate_submission about it
the five-clause advance verdict (receipt, seat execution, relations held, relations fully checked, exports available) and its blocked_by list
the honesty lines about what this receipt effectively proves on a ref-only canonical HEAD
memoizing one validation per candidate and HEAD, computed once in this process
the impact arrangement around StateRecord.closure: direct, propagated, protected, conflicts, locks and unknown coverage
the before/after/why comparison of two runs' exported objects, joined by name from retained seat-3dm-inspection records
does_not_own: the validators themselves - archflow.validation.engine
the one propagation rule - archflow.state.state_record's closure
running the candidate or reading its receipt - studio.candidate
promoting anything: nothing here writes canonical state or advances a stage
reading a .3dm - the comparison joins inspection records, never files
invariants: the receipt and the verdict are deliberately two different answers and are never merged
advance requires all five clauses; every refusal is named in blocked_by
a validation is about one candidate at one HEAD - the key includes the HEAD version
impact adds no propagation rule of its own; it calls StateRecord.closure and arranges the answer
the comparison is a join on retained records, with a stated tolerance, not browser or geometry inference
modules.notes: On a ref-only CanonicalProjectState@1 the receipt effectively proves artifact presence and base match only (P110), and says so.

modules.purpose: The candidate submission: the only boundary from speculative work to formal review.
owns: the submission record and its full content digest (CandidateSubmission.content_digest)
the delta a candidate proposes (CandidateDelta: facts, commitments, obligations, artifacts)
claims with their evidence refs (Claim)
the rule that a candidate may add only PROPOSED commitments
does_not_own: running the gates over a submission (validation.engine)
the receipt a gate run produces (validation.model)
promoting an accepted delta into canonical state (project.repository.prepare_transition)
invariants: the content digest covers the complete submission, so a receipt proves which delta was checked, not merely which id
claim keys and discharged obligation ids are unique
only PROPOSED commitments may be added by a candidate
never writes the filesystem
modules.notes: fold: '← fold'; it is the input type of validate_submission, so it can only fold together with validation/engine.py and the CanonicalState@1 path P110 retires.

modules.purpose: Policy-as-code architecture boundary checks over the source roots, driven by governance/architecture_policy.json.
owns: loading and validating ArchFlowArchitecturePolicy@1
the checked-file set for the configured roots and the single AST index per file
the checks: forbidden imports, instance-answer literals, filesystem writes outside allowed functions, forbidden framework identifiers, commit soft-gate leaks, probe-boundary executables
the Finding shape and the JSON/text report and exit code
does_not_own: the policy content - governance/architecture_policy.json
the work registry and its ledgers - tools.devctl
the module registry rules CANONICAL_SPINE 4 describes (owner-symbol, duplicate-body, archive-import) - not implemented here yet
running tests or type checks
invariants: no archflow import: the checker parses source and never executes it
a policy that cannot be interpreted deterministically fails ArchitecturePolicyError rather than passing vacuously
the file set is stable and de-duplicated, so findings are reproducible
modules.notes: No test on main (only stale bytecode in tests/__pycache__ and copies in .claude worktrees); the CANONICAL_SPINE 4 registry rules land here.

modules.purpose: Read governance/work_registry.json and render the two generated ledgers: the dynamic map and the planning index.
owns: loading ArchFlowDevelopmentRegistry@2 and its statuses (active, ready, blocked)
the readiness rule: an item is ready when no live item blocks it, and an id absent from the registry counts as finished
rendering docs/DYNAMIC_MAP.md and docs/mapping/planning/INDEX.md
does_not_own: architecture boundary enforcement - tools.archcheck
the module registry described in CANONICAL_SPINE 4, which is a separate file from work_registry.json
any archflow behaviour: it imports nothing from the package
invariants: the registry holds only unfinished work; a finished card is deleted along with its entry
both ledgers are generated, never hand-edited
modules.notes: No test on main (only stale bytecode in tests/__pycache__); pure governance tooling with no archflow imports.

modules.purpose: Validate and retain a ProjectStageWorkflow@1 through the P036 repository, and prove canonical HEAD did not move.
owns: the freeze command line (project root, run id, workflow path, create-run)
validating the workflow payload and storing the exact bytes as a record
the freeze receipt recording HEAD before and after
does_not_own: opening stage 0 or accepting a stage - archflow.state.stage_workflow and runtime.project_runner
converting legacy runs into evidence, or creating any geometry
the workflow schema itself - archflow.state.stage_workflow
invariants: the stored payload is exactly what was validated
canonical HEAD must be unchanged across the freeze, and the receipt says so
the record is authority-free
modules.notes: Deliberately small: the only way a workflow enters a project without acquiring a stage.

modules.purpose: The spine's entry point: load a project's State Record, workflow, envelope and seat pack from disk and hand them to run_project.
owns: the run-project command line (project root, run id, workflow ref, stage envelope ref, packs dir, export, workspace, powershell)
parsing a project:// record URI into a ProjectRecordRef
assembling the StageExecutionGuard from retained workflow, envelope, predecessor exit and predecessor closure records
reading an authored seat payload into a SeatSpec (_seat, reused by tools/verify_state_record.py)
does_not_own: the run itself and every record it writes - runtime.project_runner
seat semantics - capabilities.discipline_seats
creating or freezing a workflow - tools.freeze_project_stage_workflow
proving equivalence against a reference run - tools.verify_state_record
inputs: retained workflow / envelope / exit / closure records
invariants: every input is a retained record loaded by ref; the tool authors no design content
the stage guard is assembled before the runner is called, so a run cannot acquire a stage by side effect
modules.notes: Named as a spine entry point in CANONICAL_SPINE 1; no dedicated test, exercised through tests/test_project_runner.py's use of the same guard.

modules.purpose: Prove a State Record reproduces a reference runner run, recording both checks in a fresh run as state-record-equivalence.
owns: the equivalence command line (project, packs, reference run, target run, object renames)
building a self-contained harness StageExecutionGuard so the equivalence run opens its own stage
comparing the record-driven run's compiled programs and analytic object bounds against the reference run's
the state-record-equivalence receipt this run retains
does_not_own: running the project - runtime.project_runner
reading the seat pack - it reuses tools.run_project._seat
comparing saved .3dm geometry - adapters.three_dm_inspector and studio.validation's compare do that
invariants: the equivalence claim is recorded as a retained record, never printed only
the harness workflow is explicitly not a project stage advance
modules.notes: The P102 migration receipt tool; the paper's replay comparison runs through it.

modules.purpose: The read-only hard gates that turn a canonical state plus a candidate submission into a validation receipt.
owns: the validator protocol (Validator)
the artifact-presence and artifact-evidence gate (ArtifactPresentValidator)
the production claim gate compiled only from authorized hard commitments (AuthorizedCommitmentClaimsValidator)
the obligation-discharge gate (ObligationDischargeValidator)
deterministic receipt id derivation from state, submission and findings
fail-closed aggregation: base mismatch and validator exceptions become ERROR findings (validate_submission)
does_not_own: the receipt shape (validation.model)
the submission (submission.model)
promotion after a pass (project.repository.prepare_transition)
domain checks such as relations, cad readback or usability (capabilities/relation_checks.py and the archived lanes)
invariants: read-only: the gates never mutate state and never write anything
a base mismatch between the submission and the checked state is itself an ERROR finding
an exception inside a validator fails closed as a validator.exception finding
RequiredClaimsValidator is compatibility-only and refuses to gate production state
modules.notes: No archflow/ module imports it; its only production caller is the Studio API, and it reads CanonicalState@1, the HEAD shape P110 retires.

modules.purpose: The spine's validation result vocabulary: a finding, and the receipt that binds a verdict to the exact submission content checked.
owns: finding severity (Severity)
the finding value: code, message, severity, evidence refs (Finding)
the receipt binding a verdict to a submission digest and a checked state (ValidationReceipt)
the pass/fail consistency rule
does_not_own: running validators (validation.engine)
the deterministic-check envelope used by relation and stage checks (validation.contracts, the parallel being folded away)
the submission it reports on (submission.model)
invariants: passed is true exactly when no ERROR finding exists
submission_digest must be 64-hex: a receipt cannot float free of the content it checked
never writes the filesystem
modules.notes: §2.2 names Finding/ValidationReceipt the one validation result; CheckFinding/CheckReceiptEnvelope in validation/contracts.py is the parallel scheduled for deletion.
